sections.h2: Where do you record a deed in Stone County, Missouri?
sections.html:
Stone County deeds are filed at the Recorder of Deeds, 108-A East Fourth Street in Galena, the county seat. Staff answer at 417-357-6362 on weekdays from eight in the morning until four in the afternoon. Amy Larson is the elected Recorder, and the Recorder's page lists a team of deputy recorders.

Besides deeds and deeds of trust, the office files federal and state liens, military discharge papers (DD-214) and marriage license information. Marriage license applications are taken by appointment only.

Paper records held in the Galena office reach back to 1851, the year Stone County was organized. The online index starts on January 1, 1993 and runs to the present, through the iCounty portal at stonemo.icounty.com.

sections.h2: What does it cost to record a deed in Stone County?
sections.html:
Ask the office for the total on your particular deed before you mail it. Missouri law builds the price from a statutory base plus state user fees, and the final number depends on page count and the document type.

The fee picture shifted this year. The Stone County Recorder posted a release saying a flat $2.00 increase under Senate Bill 938 applied statewide from August 28, 2026, to recorded documents, marriage licenses and surveys or plats. That date is behind us, so a price list printed earlier will undercount by $2.

Recorder charges named in RSMo 59.310 for Stone County filings
ServiceStatutory amount
Recording a deed, first page$5
Recording, each added page$3
Copy of a recorded instrumentCapped at $2 for page one, $1 after
Certificate and seal outside recording$1
Release or assignment covering many items$5 for each item past the first
Subdivision plat, per sheet$25
Surcharge for a nonconforming document$25

None of these figures include the state user fees collected under RSMo 59.319, which were also rewritten by the 2026 bill.

sections.h2: How should a deed be prepared before it goes to Galena?
sections.html:
Leave three inches of blank space across the top of page one for the Recorder's stamp, and keep three-quarters of an inch clear on the other edges. A document that fails the layout test may be returned with an explanation or accepted with the $25 surcharge.

  • Print on loose white or light sheets, one side only, in black or dark ink.
  • Use type of at least eight points and type each signer's name beneath the signature.
  • Put the title, date, grantors with marital status, grantees and legal description on the first page below the blank margin.
  • Include a mailing address for at least one grantee.

The Recorder is not allowed to file a deed without a legal description or a grantee mailing address. The statute adds that constructive notice and validity are not lost when one of them is missing, but the office will still decline the filing.

sections.h2: How does the Recorder connect to Stone County property tax?
sections.html:
The Assessor maps parcel lines from warranty deeds supplied by the Recorder, so an unrecorded deed leaves the map behind. Matt Daugherty is the Assessor, at 106 East Fifth Street in Galena, with real estate staff at 417-357-6145. His office typically closes the assessment books around July 1, and taxing districts generally set rates by September 1.

Anna Burk is the Collector, working from the Historic Courthouse at 108 East Fourth Street, phone 417-357-6124. Her office announced that 2026 statements would be mailed on Friday, November 13, 2026, and that online payment would open on November 6. Bills are due by December 31 and become delinquent on January 1. Mailed checks need a postmark on or before December 31. A card payment costs 2.4 percent or $1.95, whichever is greater, and a drop box sits at the north entrance of the courthouse.

The Collector's page also states that phone payments by card are no longer taken verbally. Pay in person or use the number printed on the statement.

sections.h2: Is a senior tax freeze available in Stone County?
sections.html:
A senior property tax credit freeze exists in Missouri, and Stone County runs it through the Collector's office, where Jackie Daugherty is named as the SB190 Tax Freeze Lead. The Collector's home page currently says the application process is closed for this cycle.

A seller who qualifies should still call 417-357-6124 to ask when the next window opens and what proof the office wants. Webster County describes the same credit as a freeze on residential real estate taxes for a primary residence, not an exemption, so it does not erase the bill. The freeze does not cover personal property tax on vehicles.

Ask the Collector how a sale during the year affects an approved freeze before you sign a contract.

sections.h2: What do Census figures say about Stone County homes?
sections.html:
The Census Bureau estimated 32,503 people in Stone County on July 1, 2025, a gain of 4.6 percent over the 2020 base. Warren County grew 9.8 percent and Webster County 10.1 percent over the same stretch, so Stone is the slowest of the three.

Owners occupy 83.3 percent of homes here. A typical owned home was valued at $249,000 for 2020 to 2024, and gross rent ran $896 a month. People aged 65 and over are 33.3 percent of residents, which is nearly double Warren County's 20.5 percent.

The county lists 21,225 housing units but just 13,530 households. The gap is homes that are not a household's usual address, which is useful context for anyone selling one.

sections.h2: What is Stone County like for a seller?
sections.html:
The county covers 511 square miles in southwest Missouri, and 47 of them are water. It borders Christian, Taney and Barry counties in Missouri, plus Lawrence County and Carroll County, Arkansas. Cities include Branson West, Crane, Galena, Hurley, Kimberling City, which is the largest, and Reeds Spring. Branson sits mostly in Taney County, and Stone County was part of the Branson micropolitan area until 2023.

Census data shows how much of the local economy runs on visitors. Accommodation and food services sales were $109.9 million in 2022, against $44.3 million in Warren County and $44.1 million in Webster County. Only 49.5 percent of residents 16 and older are in the labor force.

School districts serving the county include Blue Eye R-V, Crane R-III, Galena R-II, Hurley R-I and Reeds Spring R-IV, along with the one-school Shell Knob 78 district. The district name appears on the tax statement.

sections.h2: How can an owner avoid overpaying for a copy of a deed?
sections.html:
Go to the Recorder directly. The office has warned residents about mailers from outside companies that offer a certified deed copy for $87 or more, then simply order it from the county. A copy from the Recorder is limited by statute to $2 for the first page, $1 for each added page and $1 for a certificate.

The Recorder's page also links DeedWatch.com, a free service that emails you when a document is recorded against criteria you choose. It will not prevent fraud, but it gives owners an early warning.

faqs.q: Where is the Stone County Recorder of Deeds?
faqs.a: The office is at 108-A East Fourth Street, Galena, MO 65656. Call 417-357-6362 on a weekday between eight and four.

faqs.q: Can I search Stone County deeds online?
faqs.a: Yes, from January 1, 1993 forward through the county's iCounty portal. Records before that date are in the Galena office, which holds paper records back to 1851.

faqs.q: Did Missouri recording fees go up in 2026?
faqs.a: Yes. Senate Bill 938 added a flat $2.00 starting August 28, 2026, for recorded documents, marriage licenses and plats or surveys. Ask the Recorder for the exact amount for your page count.

faqs.q: What if my deed does not meet the margin rules?
faqs.a: The Recorder can send it back with a reason or record it for an extra $25. Page one needs a three inch blank top margin.

faqs.q: When are Stone County property taxes due?
faqs.a: By December 31, with delinquency starting January 1. The 2026 statements were mailed on November 13, 2026, and the Collector's number is 417-357-6124.
